items.headline: WWT and Confluent argue production AI fails on data, not on the model
items.summary: WWT published a Nov. 20 article, written with Confluent, arguing that models are already good enough for most enterprise uses and that the harder problem is trusted, real-time data. WWT said IBM completed its acquisition of Confluent in March 2026, that WWT is a Confluent Premier Partner, and that Confluent's 2026 Data Streaming Report surveyed 4,625 IT leaders, of whom 32 percent said they have agentic AI in production and 66 percent cited data infrastructure and data quality as barriers. WWT said Confluent has dozens of customers running AI agents in production, and that its Real-Time Context Engine serves agents the latest business state over the Model Context Protocol with role-based access control and audit logging. WWT said its role is to assess data readiness, modernize the data foundation, and carry an organization through implementation.

items.headline: WWT recaps NetApp Insight, including two partner-of-the-year awards
items.summary: WWT published a Nov. 17 recap of NetApp Insight 2026. WWT said NetApp announced a renewed AI Data Engine that works across a customer's data estate, not only data stored on NetApp, after acquiring DataPelago, and that NetApp claims its Novus system delivers 100 terabytes per second and can feed 50,000 GPUs at 2 gigabytes per second each. WWT said that on Oct. 1, at Insight, NetApp named WWT its fiscal 2026 North America Partner of the Year and AI Partner of the Year. WWT also said NetApp added Oracle Cloud Infrastructure as a first-party ONTAP service, alongside AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud.
